main_text.p: [?]ctio totidem Naturæ sunt voces, quibus potentiam, sapientiam & bonitatem Creatoris eloquitur: vt eradi ex iis nequeat conditoris imago, quin penitus ipsæ aboleantur. Hi divinitatis characteres singulis impressi Naturis πολυθεότητος invehendæ occasionem gentilibus nonnullis præbuisse mihi videntur, quod nec Cicero diffitetur, 2. de natura Deorum, vbi ex Physica ratione magnam affirmat fluxisse Deorum multitudinem, qui humana in duti specie fabulas poetis suppeditarint, hominumque vitam omni superstitione referserint. Hæc Saturni, Iovis, Mercurii, Veneris, Iunonis, Vulcani, Neptuni, Minervæ, Cereris, Bacchi, Dianæ &c. origo. Vt que ex Physica ratione Deorum multitudinem profluxisse prisca oftenderet superstitio, quatuor Deorum classes constituit: in prima Cœlites, in secunda Æthereos, in tertia Marinos, in quarta Terreos collocavit: in vniuersum autem triginta millia numeravit. Nempe cum diuinitatis vbique vestigia animadverterent, Cœlum, Aerem, Maria, & Terras Diis replerunt, & pene singulis Naturæ operibus singula assignarunt Numina. Qui prudentiores è gen-tilibus fuere, ex vno Iove omnia, vnumque Iovem didicerunt[?].

page.notes: Handwritten annotations in the left margin and between lines (Greek and Latin scribbles, underlining, marks over "Terreos" and "Neptuni") are manuscript and are not transcribed. The opening word is partly covered by a handwritten mark; the first letter is uncertain. "didicerunt" is partly overwritten by handwriting. "Iovem" at the foot is the catchword. No page number is printed on this scan. Greek word πολυθεότητος is copied as read. The top-right edge shows the neighbouring page and is excluded.
